newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge union expects shift deal soon.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge union expects shift deal soon.

text.p: The union representing striking Falconbridge Ltd workers in Ontario said on Monday it was close to reaching an agreement with the mining company on shift scheduling.
While full-scale talks have not resumed since negotiations broke off on August 1, subcommittees have been trading proposals on shift scheduling.

"Presently, the subcommittees on shift scheduling are meeting and hopefully we can wrap this issue up today," Rolly Gauthier, local 598 president of the Canadian Auto Workers union, said in a telephone interview on Monday.
About 1,400 unionized workers walked off the job earlier this month at Falconbridge's Sudbury, Ontario operations.
Gauthier said last week he hoped full scale negotiations would resume this week.
"I am still hopeful that will happen," Gauthier said on Monday.
Falconbridge officials were unavailable for comment.
Falconbridge's Sudbury production last year, including custom feed, was 45,700 tonnes of nickel, 50,000 tonnes of copper and 1,600 tonnes of cobalt.

Falconbridge said last week it is adjusting the flow of nickel matte into its Kristiansand refinery in Norway to compensate for the Ontario strike and will avoid going to the spot market to meet its obligations.
